summary: Little Hebo tower, Siuslaw NF: built 1934-35 at 100-101 feet, moved to Table Mountain in 1958-59 and removed there in 1973; no source describes the Little Hebo site now.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date the tower to 1935, while 1934 newspaper items describe it being erected that year. The story keeps the register's 1935 and notes the 1934 work.
The register says steel; firelookout.com says it could have been wooden. Facts follow the register and the story flags the doubt.
The register gives 101 feet and the 1934 newspapers give 100 feet. Facts use 30.5 m (100 feet).
The Table Mountain account dates construction there to 1958 and the station's first season to 1959; the Little Hebo history and the register give the move as 1959.

notes_for_editor: No source read describes what remains at Little Hebo or Table Mountain today, or whether either is open to visitors. No staffing history was found for Little Hebo, so none is written. The FFLOS page calls the destination 'Table Lookout'; the Table Mountain sources name Table Mountain in Lincoln County, and the story uses that name. An ORWW Osbornes Project PDF on Table Mountain (Kemnow, 2020) confirms 'The lookout was removed' in 1973; it was not cited because the Oregon Lookouts page carries the same line. Oregon Digital (Siuslaw National Forest Collection, item pc289j289) has a Little Hebo Lookout image that was not opened, so no photo is added. The Table Mountain page quotes a 1958 Lincoln FPA annual report that calls the tower reassembled there 'a wooden tower' ('It is a wooden tower'); no story claim relies on it, but it bears on the steel-or-wooden conflict and is not cited here.
